neighbours.label: ' how' right after 'just' in exclamative/degree clauses ('just how close/easy/much'); pole is dense and fires weakly on much text
fire: Looking at the old photos, I never realized just how small our first apartment really was.
The new report shows just how much the city has changed over the last decade.
You might be surprised just how easy it is to bake bread at home with simple tools.
Her speech revealed just how deeply the scandal had shaken the whole team.
Nobody on the crew understood just how dangerous the storm would become by nightfall.
This chart makes clear just how quickly prices climbed after the policy change.
Standing at the edge, we finally saw just how steep the canyon walls were.
Fans were stunned to learn just how close the club came to bankruptcy last spring.
quiet: Looking at the old photos, I noticed our first apartment had green curtains everywhere.

Her speech addressed the scandal and thanked the whole team for their patience.
The crew watched the radar as the storm moved slowly toward the coast.
This chart tracks the prices of eggs and milk after the policy change.
We stood at the edge of the canyon and ate our sandwiches in silence.
The club nearly went bankrupt last spring, according to several local reporters.
